title: Command Returning Unrelated Query or Presentation Data
pattern: A command returns data that is not the outcome of its own state change: an unrelated read of other state (a heartbeat returning the peer count), a read-model or view DTO built on the write path (save returning a display model, checkout returning a receipt view), or a formatted human-readable confirmation string.
why_bad: Callers who only want the data start invoking the command to get it, triggering the mutation as a side effect of reading. Write paths become coupled to read and presentation models, so neither can change independently (the CQRS split is lost), and formatted strings returned from commands get parsed or displayed as if they were state.
detection: A method that mutates `self` or persistent state and returns a value that (a) is computed from fields or collaborators the command did not change, (b) is a read-model/view/DTO type distinct from the written entity, or (c) is a formatted `String`/markup describing the action, while a query that returns the same data exists or could exist independently.
counterexample: Returning the command's own outcome: the ID or handle of a created entity, the removed or previous value, whether the change applied, the new version for optimistic concurrency, bytes written, domain events produced, or a `Result` of these.
source: Bertrand Meyer's Command-Query Separation as presented in Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Ch. 3; Scott Wlaschin, *Domain Modeling Made Functional* (2017), Ch. 5 and 10 (CQRS); Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (2017), Ch. 8; Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020), Ch. 13.
